summary: The root نقع (nqE) primarily describes water that collects and stagnates, often changing in color or quality.
lane: 1 نَقَعَ ذ and It (water) remained, or stagnated, or collected, in a hollow, or cavity: (Mgh:) or remained long, and became altered: (Msb:) or the former [and latter] collected in a مَنْقَع : (S:) or the latter [and former] became yellow and altered. (K.) -b2- نَقَعَ and [ He macerated, steeped, or soaked, a medicine, in water, ] he left it in water until its colour became changed. (Msb.)

headwords.def: نَقَعَ and It (water) remained, or stagnated, or collected, in a hollow, or cavity: (Mgh:) or remained long, and became altered: (Msb:) or the former [and latter] collected in a مَنْقَع: (S:) or the latter [and former] became yellow and altered. (K.) نَقَعَ and [ He macerated, steeped, or soaked, a medicine, in water, ] he left it in water until its colour became changed. (Msb.)
نَقِيعٌ An infusion; meaning, a beverage made by steeping something in water: (Msb:) and a mash.
سَمٌّ نَاقِعٌ Poison that takes effect; (S, K;) that kills: (TA:) that remains fixed, (Abu-nNasr, K, TA,) and collects. (Abu-Nasr, TA.)
أَنْقَعُ More, or most, thirst-quenching: see an ex. under الحَا ُ, in art. حو; and another voce رَشَفَ.
أَنْقُوعَةٌ The hollow, or depression, of ثَرِيد, (S, A, K,) in which the gravy collects. (A, K. *)
مَنْقَعُ مَآءِ, and مَآءٍ, A place where water remains and collects; where it collects and stagnates; or where it remains long, and becomes altered. See نَقَعَ.

مَنْقَعُ البُرْمِ Untwisted old thread which a woman spins a second time, and puts into the stone cooking-pots, because she has nothing but these [ in which to deposit it ]. (Sgh, K, TA. [From the K it would seem to be مُنْقعٌ alone: and in the CK, البُرام is erroneously put for البِرام: Golius found it written البَرَام; and has wrongly explained it in his Appendix.]) سَمٌّ مُنْقَعٌ Poison made into a confection. (S, K, TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
